answer: Divergent challenge protocol: each identity must answer a fresh random challenge whose correct response depends on a secret only that identity holds, so copies inherit nothing usable. Every clone either guesses (and fails) or must acquire its own secret through a costly private channel, paying the full acquisition cost again per copy rather than sharing one. An attacker who tries to whisper answers between clones leaks the link, collapsing the apparent distinctness at the next summit of verification. Scaling to an orchard of valid identities therefore costs linearly, not once.
